title: Symmetry and Monotonicity of the Scaled Cubic y = x^3 / 8
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Describe the graph of y = x^3 / 8, identify its symmetry, and state the intervals on which the function is increasing and where it is decreasing.
finalAnswer: \text{Symmetric about the origin; Increasing on } (-\infty, \infty); \text{ Decreasing nowhere}

steps.title: Test for Origin Symmetry
steps.explanation: Since f(-x) = -f(x) for all real numbers x, the function is odd and its graph is symmetric with respect to the origin.
steps.why: Odd integer powers preserve negation, making any constant multiple of x^3 an odd function.

steps.title: Analyze Monotonicity Across (-inf, inf)
steps.explanation: For any real numbers x_1 < x_2, we have x_1^3 < x_2^3, and dividing by the positive constant 8 preserves the strict inequality.
steps.why: Scaling a strictly increasing function by a positive constant preserves its strict monotonicity.

steps.title: State the Monotonicity Intervals
steps.explanation: The graph is a vertically compressed cubic curve passing through (-2, -1), (0, 0), and (2, 1), rising across the entire real line (-inf, inf).
steps.why: The function increases over its entire domain (-inf, inf) with a horizontal inflection point at the origin.
